notes: Phases 1 (Inciting Threat / Assignment), 5 (Capture / Confrontation & Reveal), and 7 (Final Assault) are fully populated with real examples per the deliverable spec. Phases 2,3,4,6,8 include structural stubs (purpose + required + a starter option) ready for the same population pattern.

story_phases.purpose: Establish a threat of real consequence and put Bond on it, whether by institutional order or personal cause.

options.name: Official M Briefing - Missing Agents
options.description: M reports MI6 operatives have gone dark in a specific region; Bond is assigned to find out why.

details.initial_threat_visibility: obscured - Bond must discover the real scheme

options.name: Honey-Trap Bait Recognized as Trap
options.description: An enemy service dangles a defector and a valuable object (decoder, formula) as bait, and Bond is sent in with eyes open, knowing it's likely a trap.

details.initial_threat_visibility: partially known - bait is obvious, mechanism of betrayal is not

options.name: Stolen WMD Ultimatum
options.description: A criminal organization steals a weapon of mass consequence (nuclear device, warheads) and issues a ransom threat against a government or the world.

details.authority: M / MI6, often in concert with allied agency
details.initial_threat_visibility: fully known target, unknown perpetrator location

options.name: Personal Vendetta - No Institutional Sanction
options.description: A villain harms Bond or someone close to him directly (maiming/killing an ally); Bond acts without, or in defiance of, official authorization.

details.initial_threat_visibility: fully known villain, unknown full operation

options.name: Compromised Bond as the Initial Threat
options.description: Bond himself is brainwashed or discredited and must be deprogrammed/redeemed before being pointed at the real villain.
source_works: The Man with the Golden Gun (novel)

details.authority: M / MI6, but trust is the plot question
details.sanction_level: conditional - mission doubles as loyalty test
details.initial_threat_visibility: Bond's own reliability is the initial unknown

story_phases.purpose: Bond relocates to unfamiliar territory and gathers intel through a local ally who supplies what Bond can't get alone.

options.name: Station Chief / Local Contact Network
options.description: Bond works with an established local ally (station chief, foreign colleague) to map the terrain before contact.

story_phases.phase_name: First Contact with the Villain's World
story_phases.purpose: A social or competitive set piece brings Bond briefly into the villain's orbit without full exposure; a plot-relevant woman is introduced.

options.name: Competitive Game as Reconnaissance
options.description: Cards, golf, or another game of skill lets Bond observe and needle the villain in a controlled social setting.

story_phases.purpose: The villain's side tries to eliminate, warn off, or test Bond; this scene sets the story's violence register.

options.name: Assassination Attempt via Trusted Ally
options.description: Someone Bond has reason to trust turns out to be the threat, revealed mid-escalation.
source_works: The Spy Who Loved Me (1977, inverted as rival-turned-ally)

story_phases.purpose: Bond meets the villain directly and the full scheme is disclosed to Bond and the audience - the genre's most load-bearing beat.

options.name: Recruit-From-Within Reveal
options.description: The villain, instead of killing Bond outright, folds him into the operation, disclosing the plan as part of recruiting or testing his usefulness.

details.reveal_mechanism: verbal recruitment pitch + demonstration of the plan's mechanics
details.narrative_function: collapses reveal (phase 5) and turn (phase 6) into one continuous sequence

options.name: Dinner-Table Monologue in the Lair
options.description: Bond is captured and hosted (dinner, tour of the base) while the villain explains the scheme at length, savoring the reveal.

details.reveal_mechanism: extended monologue, often with visual aids (models, screens, the lair itself)
details.bond_status: fully captive, no agency until phase 6
details.narrative_function: maximizes spectacle and villain characterization before the turn

options.name: Endurance Test / Torture as Confrontation
options.description: The villain confronts Bond not with words but with a physical ordeal (torture, gauntlet, laser) that itself reveals the villain's nature.
source_works: Licence to Kill (1989, near-death by decompression/shark)

details.reveal_mechanism: the method of the ordeal itself characterizes the villain; scheme details may come before or after
details.bond_status: captive and in immediate physical danger
details.narrative_function: raises stakes viscerally rather than expositorily; often the point where tone (grim vs. stylized) is fixed for the rest of the story

options.name: Ambiguous Threat Without Full Capture
options.description: Bond confronts the villain's agent (not the villain personally) and the scheme is only partially revealed, leaving real ambiguity into the final act.

details.reveal_mechanism: fragmentary - full picture withheld from Bond and/or audience until later
details.narrative_function: sustains tension into the final phases instead of resolving it at the reveal

story_phases.purpose: Bond breaks free and the story pivots from reactive to proactive.

options.name: Gadget-Enabled Escape
options.description: A previously established gadget (or one improvised on the spot) provides the means of escape.

story_phases.purpose: A large-scale confrontation destroys or defeats the villain's operational base, not just the villain personally.

options.name: Allied Mass Assault on the Lair
options.description: An allied force (commandos, ninjas, local militia) storms the villain's base in a large multi-combatant battle while Bond handles the villain personally.

details.location_type: villain's mega-lair (volcano, undersea base, space station, circus/train)
details.outcome_mechanism: base destroyed by the allied force while Bond neutralizes the villain in a parallel personal confrontation

options.name: One-on-One Duel
options.description: The climax is a formal duel between Bond and a single, skilled adversary, without a mass battle.
source_works: The Man with the Golden Gun (novel)
The Man with the Golden Gun (1974)

details.outcome_mechanism: direct personal victory, no supporting force required

options.name: Vehicular Mass Finale
options.description: The climax plays out across a chase or battle among vehicles (tanker convoy, submarines, ski chase) rather than a fixed lair assault.
source_works: On Her Majesty's Secret Service (1969, ski/bobsled chase)

details.location_type: open terrain, sea, or road network
details.outcome_mechanism: villain's operation is destroyed via pursuit/destruction of moving assets rather than a static base

options.name: Infiltration-Sabotage from Within
options.description: Having been embedded in the operation (per a Phase 5 recruit-from-within reveal), Bond sabotages the plan from inside as it's underway, rather than mounting an external assault.

details.scale: variable, often escalates into a mass finale once sabotage is discovered
details.location_type: the operation's own facility (vault, processing plant)
details.outcome_mechanism: plan collapses from internal sabotage, frequently triggering a secondary mass confrontation as cover is blown

story_phases.purpose: The threat is closed out and tension releases, most often through romance, occasionally through tragedy or irony.

options.name: Triumphant Romantic Coda
options.description: Bond and the Bond Girl are alone together, danger past, ending on wit or romance.

options.name: Tragic Coda
options.description: Victory over the villain is undercut by a personal loss inflicted in the final scene.

elements.name: Signature vehicle gadget (ejector seat, submarine car)
Silent, physically overwhelming henchman with a signature kill method
source_works: The Spy Who Loved Me / Moonraker (Jaws)

elements.name: No standout henchman - villain acts directly or via anonymous force
source_works: From Russia with Love (1963, Grant is closer to a co-lead antagonist)

elements.name: Asia (Hong Kong, Japan, Thailand)
source_works: The Man with the Golden Gun

elements.name: Full cultural disguise (dress, makeup, assumed identity)
Comic costume disguise used for tension release then reveal
Broad comic set pieces and recurring comic characters (e.g. Sheriff Pepper)
source_works: The Man with the Golden Gun

elements.name: Fully sanctioned MI6 mission with Q-branch and M support throughout
Unofficial/rogue action, license revoked, support arrives informally if at all
Car chase with gadget-vehicle
source_works: The Man with the Golden Gun

compatibility_rules.description: A Phase 1 'Personal Vendetta' mission origin combined with a 'Broad comic set pieces' comic-relief level tends to undercut stakes, since camp tone signals low real risk while revenge plots require the opposite. Flag, do not block.
conflicting_options: Broad comic set pieces and recurring comic characters

compatibility_rules.description: Withdrawing institutional backing (Phase 1) while retaining heavy Q-branch gadget dependence creates a credibility gap, since gadgets imply institutional support the story has withdrawn. Flag, do not block.
conflicting_options: Signature vehicle gadget (ejector seat, submarine car)

compatibility_rules.description: A tragic Phase 8 coda paired with a highly stylized/comic recurring henchman can feel tonally split. Historically rare but not attempted in the corpus - flag as an untested combination rather than a proven conflict.
conflicting_options: Silent, physically overwhelming henchman with a signature kill method
